units.leftText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the assembly of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in the whole of Achaia:
units.rightText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints that are in the whole of Achaia:

units.leftText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort,
units.rightText: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;

units.leftText: who comforts us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort those who are in any affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
units.rightText: who comforteth us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort them that are in any affliction, through the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.

units.leftText: For as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, even so our comfort also abounds through Christ.
units.rightText: For as the sufferings of Christ abound unto us, even so our comfort also aboundeth through Christ.

units.leftText: But if we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which produces in you the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer.
units.rightText: But whether we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; or whether we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which worketh in the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer:

units.leftText: Our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that, since you are partakers of the sufferings, so you are also of the comfort.
units.rightText: and our hope for you is stedfast; knowing that, as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so also are ye of the comfort.

units.leftText: For we don’t desire to have you uninformed, brothers, concerning our affliction which happened to us in Asia: that we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power, so much that we despaired even of life.
units.rightText: For we would not have you ignorant, brethren, concerning our affliction which befell us in Asia, that we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power, insomuch that we despaired even of life:
leftNotes: 1:8 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Yes, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead,
units.rightText: yea, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raiseth the dead:

units.leftText: who delivered us out of so great a death, and does deliver, on whom we have set our hope that he will also still deliver us,
units.rightText: who delivered us out of so great a death, and will deliver: on whom we have set our hope that he will also still deliver us;

units.leftText: you also helping together on our behalf by your supplication; that, for the gift given to us by means of many, thanks may be given by many persons on your behalf.
units.rightText: ye also helping together on our behalf by your supplication; that, for the gift bestowed upon us by means of many, thanks may be given by many persons on our behalf.
leftNotes: 1:11 + MT: your; TR and NU: our

units.leftText: For our boasting is this: the testimony of our conscience that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, we behaved ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you.
units.rightText: For our glorying is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, we behaved ourselves in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward.

units.leftText: For we write no other things to you than what you read or even acknowledge, and I hope you will acknowledge to the end—
units.rightText: For we write no other things unto you, than what ye read or even acknowledge, and I hope ye will acknowledge unto the end:

units.leftText: as also you acknowledged us in part—that we are your boasting, even as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.
units.rightText: as also ye did acknowledge us in part, that we are your glorying, even as ye also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.

units.leftText: In this confidence, I was determined to come first to you, that you might have a second benefit,
units.rightText: And in this confidence I was minded to come first unto you, that ye might have a second benefit;

units.leftText: and by you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and to be sent forward by you on my journey to Judea.
units.rightText: and by you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come unto you, and of you to be set forward on my journey unto Judæa.

units.leftText: When I therefore planned this, did I show fickleness? Or the things that I plan, do I plan according to the flesh, that with me there should be the “Yes, yes” and the “No, no?”
units.rightText: When I therefore was thus minded, did I show fickleness? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be the yea yea and the nay nay?

units.leftText: But as God is faithful, our word toward you was not “Yes and no.”
units.rightText: But as God is faithful, our word toward you is not yea and nay.

units.leftText: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us—by me, Silvanus, and Timothy—was not “Yes and no,” but in him is “Yes.”
units.rightText: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not yea and nay, but in him is yea.

units.leftText: For however many are the promises of God, in him is the “Yes.” Therefore also through him is the “Amen”, to the glory of God through us.
units.rightText: For how many soever be the promises of God, in him is the yea: wherefore also through him is the Amen, unto the glory of God through us.

units.leftText: Now he who establishes us with you in Christ and anointed us is God,
units.rightText: Now he that establisheth us with you in Christ, and anointed us, is God;

units.leftText: who also sealed us and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.
units.rightText: who also sealed us, and gave us the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.

units.leftText: But I call God for a witness to my soul, that to spare you, I didn’t come to Corinth.
units.rightText: But I call God for a witness upon my soul, that to spare you I forbare to come unto Corinth.

units.leftText: We don’t control your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy. For you stand firm in faith.
units.rightText: Not that we have lordship over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for in faith ye stand fast.

units.leftText: But I determined this for myself, that I would not come to you again in sorrow.
units.rightText: But I determined this for myself, that I would not come again to you with sorrow.

units.leftText: For if I make you grieve, then who will make me glad but he who is made to grieve by me?
units.rightText: For if I make you sorry, who then is he that maketh me glad but he that is made sorry by me?

units.leftText: And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I came, I wouldn’t have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all that my joy would be shared by all of you.
units.rightText: And I wrote this very thing, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.

units.leftText: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not that you should be made to grieve, but that you might know the love that I have so abundantly for you.
units.rightText: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be made sorry, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you.

units.leftText: But if any has caused sorrow, he has caused sorrow not to me, but in part (that I not press too heavily) to you all.
units.rightText: But if any hath caused sorrow, he hath caused sorrow, not to me, but in part (that I press not too heavily) to you all.

units.leftText: This punishment which was inflicted by the many is sufficient for such a one;
units.rightText: Sufficient to such a one is this punishment which was inflicted by the many;

units.leftText: so that, on the contrary, you should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a one should be swallowed up with his excessive sorrow.
units.rightText: so that contrariwise ye should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a one should be swallowed up with his overmuch sorrow.

units.leftText: Therefore I beg you to confirm your love toward him.
units.rightText: Wherefore I beseech you to confirm your love toward him.

units.leftText: For to this end I also wrote, that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.
units.rightText: For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye are obedient in all things.

units.leftText: Now I also forgive whomever you forgive anything. For if indeed I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven that one for your sakes in the presence of Christ,
units.rightText: But to whom ye forgive anything, I forgive also: for what I also have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, for your sakes have I forgiven it in the presence of Christ;

units.leftText: that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan, for we are not ignorant of his schemes.
units.rightText: that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan: for we are not ignorant of his devices.

units.leftText: Now when I came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, and when a door was opened to me in the Lord,
units.rightText: Now when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and when a door was opened unto me in the Lord,

units.leftText: I had no relief for my spirit, because I didn’t find Titus my brother, but taking my leave of them, I went out into Macedonia.
units.rightText: I had no relief for my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went forth into Macedonia.

units.leftText: Now thanks be to God who always leads us in triumph in Christ, and reveals through us the sweet aroma of his knowledge in every place.
units.rightText: But thanks be unto God, who always leadeth us in triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest through us the savor of his knowledge in every place.

units.leftText: For we are a sweet aroma of Christ to God in those who are being saved and in those who perish:
units.rightText: For we are a sweet savor of Christ unto God, in them that are saved, and in them that perish;

units.leftText: to the one a stench from death to death, to the other a sweet aroma from life to life. Who is sufficient for these things?
units.rightText: to the one a savor from death unto death; to the other a savor from life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?

units.leftText: For we are not as so many, peddling the word of God. But as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, we speak in Christ.
units.rightText: For we are not as the many, corrupting the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, speak we in Christ.

units.leftText: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as do some, letters of commendation to you or from you?
units.rightText: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? or need we, as do some, epistles of commendation to you or from you?

units.leftText: You are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read by all men,
units.rightText: Ye are our epistle, written in our hearts, known and read of all men;

units.leftText: being revealed that you are a letter of Christ, served by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tablets of stone, but in tablets that are hearts of flesh.
units.rightText: being made manifest that ye are an epistle of Christ, ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in tables that are hearts of flesh.

units.leftText: Such confidence we have through Christ toward God,
units.rightText: And such confidence have we through Christ to God-ward:

units.leftText: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God,
units.rightText: not that we are sufficient of ourselves, to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God;

units.leftText: who also made us sufficient as servants of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
units.rightText: who also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.

units.leftText: But if the service of death, written engraved on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look steadfastly on the face of Moses for the glory of his face, which was passing away,
units.rightText: But if the ministration of death, written, and engraven on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look stedfastly upon the face of Moses for the glory of his face; which glory was passing away:

units.leftText: won’t service of the Spirit be with much more glory?
units.rightText: how shall not rather the ministration of the spirit be with glory?

units.leftText: For if the service of condemnation has glory, the service of righteousness exceeds much more in glory.
units.rightText: For if the ministration of condemnation hath glory, much rather doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

units.leftText: For most certainly that which has been made glorious has not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasses.
units.rightText: For verily that which hath been made glorious hath not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasseth.

units.leftText: For if that which passes away was with glory, much more that which remains is in glory.
units.rightText: For if that which passeth away was with glory, much more that which remaineth is in glory.

units.leftText: Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,
units.rightText: Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,

units.leftText: and not as Moses, who put a veil on his face so that the children of Israel wouldn’t look steadfastly on the end of that which was passing away.
units.rightText: and are not as Moses, who put a veil upon his face, that the children of Israel should not look stedfastly on the end of that which was passing away:

units.leftText: But their minds were hardened, for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains, because in Christ it passes away.
units.rightText: but their minds were hardened: for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remaineth, it not being revealed to them that it is done away in Christ.

units.leftText: But to this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart.
units.rightText: But unto this day, whensoever Moses is read, a veil lieth upon their heart.

units.leftText: But whenever someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
units.rightText: But whensoever it shall turn to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

units.leftText: Now the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
units.rightText: Now the Lord is the Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

units.leftText: But we all, with unveiled face seeing the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, the Spirit.
units.rightText: But we all, with unveiled face beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord the Spirit.

units.leftText: Therefore, seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we don’t faint.
units.rightText: Therefore seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we faint not:

units.leftText: But we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness nor handling the word of God deceitfully, but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
units.rightText: but we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

units.leftText: Even if our Good News is veiled, it is veiled in those who are dying,
units.rightText: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled in them that perish:

units.leftText: in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, that the light of the Good News of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not dawn on them.
units.rightText: in whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of the unbelieving, that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not dawn upon them.

units.leftText: For we don’t preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake,
units.rightText: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.

units.leftText: seeing it is God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: Seeing it is God, that said, Light shall shine out of darkness, who shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God and not from ourselves.
units.rightText: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves;

units.leftText: We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair;
units.rightText: we are pressed on every side, yet not straitened; perplexed, yet not unto despair;

units.leftText: pursued, yet not forsaken; struck down, yet not destroyed;
units.rightText: pursued, yet not forsaken; smitten down, yet not destroyed;

units.leftText: always carrying in the body the putting to death of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
units.rightText: always bearing about in the body the dying of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be manifested in our body.

units.leftText: For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
units.rightText: For we who live are always delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be manifested in our mortal flesh.

units.leftText: So then death works in us, but life in you.
units.rightText: So then death worketh in us, but life in you.

units.leftText: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, “I believed, and therefore I spoke.” We also believe, and therefore we also speak,
units.rightText: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, I believed, and therefore did I speak; we also believe, and therefore also we speak;

units.leftText: knowing that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also through Jesus, and will present us with you.
units.rightText: knowing that he that raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also with Jesus, and shall present us with you.
leftNotes: 4:14 NU reads with instead of through.

units.leftText: For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.
units.rightText: For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound unto the glory of God.

units.leftText: Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day.
units.rightText: Wherefore we faint not; but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.

units.leftText: For our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory,
units.rightText: For our light affliction, which is for the moment, worketh for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory;

units.leftText: while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
units.rightText: while we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

units.leftText: For we know that if the earthly house of our tent is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.
units.rightText: For we know that if the earthly house of our tabernacle be dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.

units.leftText: For most certainly in this we groan, longing to be clothed with our habitation which is from heaven,
units.rightText: For verily in this we groan, longing to be clothed upon with our habitation which is from heaven:

units.leftText: if indeed being clothed, we will not be found naked.
units.rightText: if so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.

units.leftText: For indeed we who are in this tent do groan, being burdened, not that we desire to be unclothed, but that we desire to be clothed, that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
units.rightText: For indeed we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened; not for that we would be unclothed, but that we would be clothed upon, that what is mortal may be swallowed up of life.

units.leftText: Now he who made us for this very thing is God, who also gave to us the down payment of the Spirit.
units.rightText: Now he that wrought us for this very thing is God, who gave unto us the earnest of the Spirit.

units.leftText: Therefore we are always confident and know that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord;
units.rightText: Being therefore always of good courage, and knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord

units.leftText: for we walk by faith, not by sight.
units.rightText: (for we walk by faith, not by sight);

units.leftText: We are courageous, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body and to be at home with the Lord.
units.rightText: we are of good courage, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be at home with the Lord.

units.leftText: Therefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well pleasing to him.
units.rightText: Wherefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well-pleasing unto him.

units.leftText: For we must all be revealed before the judgment seat of Christ that each one may receive the things in the body according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
units.rightText: For we must all be made manifest before the judgment-seat of Christ; that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he hath done, whether it be good or bad.

units.leftText: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are revealed to God, and I hope that we are revealed also in your consciences.
units.rightText: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are made manifest unto God; and I hope that we are made manifest also in your consciences.

units.leftText: For we are not commending ourselves to you again, but speak as giving you occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may have something to answer those who boast in appearance and not in heart.
units.rightText: We are not again commending ourselves unto you, but speak as giving you occasion of glorying on our behalf, that ye may have wherewith to answer them that glory in appearance, and not in heart.

units.leftText: For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God. Or if we are of sober mind, it is for you.
units.rightText: For whether we are beside ourselves, it is unto God; or whether we are of sober mind, it is unto you.

units.leftText: For the love of Christ compels us; because we judge thus: that one died for all, therefore all died.
units.rightText: For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that one died for all, therefore all died;

units.leftText: He died for all, that those who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who for their sakes died and rose again.
units.rightText: and he died for all, that they that live should no longer live unto themselves, but unto him who for their sakes died and rose again.

units.leftText: Therefore we know no one according to the flesh from now on. Even though we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.
units.rightText: Wherefore we henceforth know no man after the flesh: even though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.

units.leftText: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
units.rightText: Wherefore if any man is in Christ, he is a new creature: the old things are passed away; behold, they are become new.
leftNotes: 5:17 “Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;
units.rightText: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ, and gave unto us the ministry of reconciliation;

units.leftText: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.
units.rightText: to wit, that God was in Christ reconciling the world unto himself, not reckoning unto them their trespasses, and having committed unto us the word of reconciliation.

units.leftText: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
units.rightText: We are ambassadors therefore on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beseech you on behalf of Christ, be ye reconciled to God.

units.leftText: For him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
units.rightText: Him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf; that we might become the righteousness of God in him.

units.leftText: Working together, we entreat also that you do not receive the grace of God in vain.
units.rightText: And working together with him we entreat also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain

units.leftText: For he says,
units.rightText: (for he saith,

units.leftText: We give no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our service may not be blamed,
units.rightText: giving no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our ministration be not blamed;

units.leftText: but in everything commending ourselves as servants of God: in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
units.rightText: but in everything commending ourselves, as ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,

units.leftText: in beatings, in imprisonments, in riots, in labors, in watchings, in fastings,
units.rightText: in stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labors, in watchings, in fastings;

units.leftText: in pureness, in knowledge, in perseverance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in sincere love,
units.rightText: in pureness, in knowledge, in longsuffering, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love unfeigned,

units.leftText: in the word of truth, in the power of God, by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,
units.rightText: in the word of truth, in the power of God; by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,

units.leftText: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report, as deceivers and yet true,
units.rightText: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true;

units.leftText: as unknown and yet well known, as dying and behold—we live, as punished and not killed,
units.rightText: as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed;

units.leftText: as sorrowful yet always rejoicing, as poor yet making many rich, as having nothing and yet possessing all things.
units.rightText: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.

units.leftText: Our mouth is open to you, Corinthians. Our heart is enlarged.
units.rightText: Our mouth is open unto you, O Corinthians, our heart is enlarged.

units.leftText: You are not restricted by us, but you are restricted by your own affections.
units.rightText: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own affections.

units.leftText: Now in return—I speak as to my children—you also open your hearts.
units.rightText: Now for a recompense in like kind (I speak as unto my children), be ye also enlarged.

units.leftText: Don’t be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship do righteousness and iniquity have? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
units.rightText: Be not unequally yoked with unbelievers: for what fellowship have righteousness and iniquity? or what communion hath light with darkness?

units.leftText: What agreement does Christ have with Belial? Or what portion does a believer have with an unbeliever?
units.rightText: And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what portion hath a believer with an unbeliever?

units.leftText: What agreement does a temple of God have with idols? For you are a temple of the living God. Even as God said, “I will dwell in them and walk in them. I will be their God and they will be my people.”
units.rightText: And what agreement hath a temple of God with idols? for we are a temple of the living God; even as God said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

units.leftText: Therefore
units.rightText: Wherefore

units.leftText: I will be to you a Father.
units.rightText: And will be to you a Father,

units.leftText: Having therefore these promises, beloved, let’s cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
units.rightText: Having therefore these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

units.leftText: Open your hearts to us. We wronged no one. We corrupted no one. We took advantage of no one.
units.rightText: Open your hearts to us: we wronged no man, we corrupted no man, we took advantage of no man.

units.leftText: I say this not to condemn you, for I have said before that you are in our hearts to die together and live together.
units.rightText: I say it not to condemn you: for I have said before, that ye are in our hearts to die together and live together.

units.leftText: Great is my boldness of speech toward you. Great is my boasting on your behalf. I am filled with comfort. I overflow with joy in all our affliction.
units.rightText: Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying on your behalf: I am filled with comfort, I overflow with joy in all our affliction.

units.leftText: For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side. Fightings were outside. Fear was inside.
units.rightText: For even when we were come into Macedonia our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, he who comforts the lowly, God, comforted us by the coming of Titus,
units.rightText: Nevertheless he that comforteth the lowly, even God, comforted us by the coming of Titus;

units.leftText: and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you while he told us of your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced still more.
units.rightText: and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort wherewith he was comforted in you, while he told us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me; so that I rejoiced yet more.

units.leftText: For though I grieved you with my letter, I do not regret it, though I did regret it. For I see that my letter made you grieve, though just for a while.
units.rightText: For though I made you sorry with my epistle, I do not regret it: though I did regret it (for I see that that epistle made you sorry, though but for a season),

units.leftText: I now rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved to repentance. For you were grieved in a godly way, that you might suffer loss by us in nothing.
units.rightText: I now rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye were made sorry unto repentance; for ye were made sorry after a godly sort, that ye might suffer loss by us in nothing.

units.leftText: For godly sorrow produces repentance leading to salvation, which brings no regret. But the sorrow of the world produces death.
units.rightText: For godly sorrow worketh repentance unto salvation, a repentance which bringeth no regret: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

units.leftText: For behold, this same thing, that you were grieved in a godly way, what earnest care it worked in you. Yes, what defense, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, and vindication! In everything you demonstrated yourselves to be pure in the matter.
units.rightText: For behold, this selfsame thing, that ye were made sorry after a godly sort, what earnest care it wrought in you, yea what clearing of yourselves, yea what indignation, yea what fear, yea what longing, yea what zeal, yea what avenging! In everything ye approved yourselves to be pure in the matter.

units.leftText: So although I wrote to you, I wrote not for his cause that did the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered the wrong, but that your earnest care for us might be revealed in you in the sight of God.
units.rightText: So although I wrote unto you, I wrote not for his cause that did the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered the wrong, but that your earnest care for us might be made manifest unto you in the sight of God.

units.leftText: Therefore we have been comforted. In our comfort we rejoiced the more exceedingly for the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by you all.
units.rightText: Therefore we have been comforted: and in our comfort we joyed the more exceedingly for the joy of Titus, because his spirit hath been refreshed by you all.

units.leftText: For if in anything I have boasted to him on your behalf, I was not disappointed. But as we spoke all things to you in truth, so our glorying also which I made before Titus was found to be truth.
units.rightText: For if in anything I have gloried to him on your behalf, I was not put to shame; but as we spake all things to you in truth, so our glorying also which I made before Titus was found to be truth.

units.leftText: His affection is more abundantly toward you, while he remembers all of your obedience, how with fear and trembling you received him.
units.rightText: And his affection is more abundantly toward you, while he remembereth the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling ye received him.

units.leftText: I rejoice that in everything I am confident concerning you.
units.rightText: I rejoice that in everything I am of good courage concerning you.

units.leftText: Moreover, brothers, we make known to you the grace of God which has been given in the assemblies of Macedonia,
units.rightText: Moreover, brethren, we make known to you the grace of God which hath been given in the churches of Macedonia;

units.leftText: how in a severe ordeal of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded to the riches of their generosity.
units.rightText: how that in much proof of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.

units.leftText: For according to their power, I testify, yes and beyond their power, they gave of their own accord,
units.rightText: For according to their power, I bear witness, yea and beyond their power, they gave of their own accord,

units.leftText: begging us with much entreaty to receive this grace and the fellowship in the service to the saints.
units.rightText: beseeching us with much entreaty in regard of this grace and the fellowship in the ministering to the saints:

units.leftText: This was not as we had expected, but first they gave their own selves to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.
units.rightText: and this, not as we had hoped, but first they gave their own selves to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.

units.leftText: So we urged Titus, that as he had made a beginning before, so he would also complete in you this grace.
units.rightText: Insomuch that we exhorted Titus, that as he had made a beginning before, so he would also complete in you this grace also.

units.leftText: But as you abound in everything—in faith, utterance, knowledge, all earnestness, and in your love to us—see that you also abound in this grace.
units.rightText: But as ye abound in everything, in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all earnestness, and in your love to us, see that ye abound in this grace also.

units.leftText: I speak not by way of commandment, but as proving through the earnestness of others the sincerity also of your love.
units.rightText: I speak not by way of commandment, but as proving through the earnestness of others the sincerity also of your love.

units.leftText: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might become rich.
units.rightText: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might become rich.

units.leftText: I give advice in this: it is expedient for you who were the first to start a year ago, not only to do, but also to be willing.
units.rightText: And herein I give my judgment: for this is expedient for you, who were the first to make a beginning a year ago, not only to do, but also to will.

units.leftText: But now complete the doing also, that as there was the readiness to be willing, so there may be the completion also out of your ability.
units.rightText: But now complete the doing also; that as there was the readiness to will, so there may be the completion also out of your ability.

units.leftText: For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according to what you have, not according to what you don’t have.
units.rightText: For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according as a man hath, not according as he hath not.

units.leftText: For this is not that others may be eased and you distressed,
units.rightText: For I say not this that others may be eased and ye distressed;

units.leftText: but for equality. Your abundance at this present time supplies their lack, that their abundance also may become a supply for your lack, that there may be equality.
units.rightText: but by equality: your abundance being a supply at this present time for their want, that their abundance also may become a supply for your want; that there may be equality:

units.leftText: As it is written, “He who gathered much had nothing left over, and he who gathered little had no lack.”
units.rightText: as it is written, He that gathered much had nothing over; and he that gathered little had no lack.

units.leftText: But thanks be to God, who puts the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus.
units.rightText: But thanks be to God, who putteth the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus.

units.leftText: For he indeed accepted our exhortation, but being himself very earnest, he went out to you of his own accord.
units.rightText: For he accepted indeed our exhortation; but being himself very earnest, he went forth unto you of his own accord.

units.leftText: We have sent together with him the brother whose praise in the Good News is known throughout all the assemblies.
units.rightText: And we have sent together with him the brother whose praise in the gospel is spread through all the churches;

units.leftText: Not only so, but he was also appointed by the assemblies to travel with us in this grace, which is served by us to the glory of the Lord himself, and to show our readiness.
units.rightText: and not only so, but who was also appointed by the churches to travel with us in the matter of this grace, which is ministered by us to the glory of the Lord, and to show our readiness:

units.leftText: We are avoiding this, that any man should blame us concerning this abundance which is administered by us.
units.rightText: avoiding this, that any man should blame us in the matter of this bounty which is ministered by us:

units.leftText: Having regard for honorable things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
units.rightText: for we take thought for things honorable, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

units.leftText: We have sent with them our brother whom we have many times proved earnest in many things, but now much more earnest, by reason of the great confidence which he has in you.
units.rightText: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have many times proved earnest in many things, but now much more earnest, by reason of the great confidence which he hath in you.

units.leftText: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker for you. As for our brothers, they are the apostles of the assemblies, the glory of Christ.
units.rightText: Whether any inquire about Titus, he is my partner and my fellow-worker to you-ward; or our brethren, they are the messengers of the churches, they are the glory of Christ.

units.leftText: Therefore show the proof of your love to them before the assemblies, and of our boasting on your behalf.
units.rightText: Show ye therefore unto them in the face of the churches the proof of your love, and of our glorying on your behalf.

units.leftText: It is indeed unnecessary for me to write to you concerning the service to the saints,
units.rightText: For as touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you:

units.leftText: for I know your readiness, of which I boast on your behalf to those of Macedonia, that Achaia has been prepared for the past year. Your zeal has stirred up very many of them.
units.rightText: for I know your readiness, of which I glory on your behalf to them of Macedonia, that Achaia hath been prepared for a year past; and your zeal hath stirred up very many of them.

units.leftText: But I have sent the brothers so that our boasting on your behalf may not be in vain in this respect, that, just as I said, you may be prepared,
units.rightText: But I have sent the brethren, that our glorying on your behalf may not be made void in this respect; that, even as I said, ye may be prepared:

units.leftText: lest by any means, if anyone from Macedonia comes there with me and finds you unprepared, we (to say nothing of you) would be disappointed in this confident boasting.
units.rightText: lest by any means, if there come with me any of Macedonia and find you unprepared, we (that we say not, ye) should be put to shame in this confidence.

units.leftText: I thought it necessary therefore to entreat the brothers that they would go before to you and arrange ahead of time the generous gift that you promised before, that the same might be ready as a matter of generosity, and not of greediness.
units.rightText: I thought it necessary therefore to entreat the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your aforepromised bounty, that the same might be ready as a matter of bounty, and not of extortion.

units.leftText: Remember this: he who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. He who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
units.rightText: But this I say, He that soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he that soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.

units.leftText: Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
units.rightText: Let each man do according as he hath purposed in his heart: not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

units.leftText: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, that you, always having all sufficiency in everything, may abound to every good work.
units.rightText: And God is able to make all grace abound unto you; that ye, having always all sufficiency in everything, may abound unto every good work:

units.leftText: As it is written,
units.rightText: as it is written,

units.leftText: Now may he who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food, supply and multiply your seed for sowing, and increase the fruits of your righteousness,
units.rightText: And he that supplieth seed to the sower and bread for food, shall supply and multiply your seed for sowing, and increase the fruits of your righteousness:

units.leftText: you being enriched in everything for all generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us.
units.rightText: ye being enriched in everything unto all liberality, which worketh through us thanksgiving to God.

units.leftText: For this service of giving that you perform not only makes up for lack among the saints, but abounds also through much giving of thanks to God,
units.rightText: For the ministration of this service not only filleth up the measure of the wants of the saints, but aboundeth also through many thanksgivings unto God;

units.leftText: seeing that through the proof given by this service, they glorify God for the obedience of your confession to the Good News of Christ and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all,
units.rightText: seeing that through the proving of you by this ministration they glorify God for the obedience of your confession unto the gospel of Christ, and for the liberality of your contribution unto them and unto all;

units.leftText: while they themselves also, with supplication on your behalf, yearn for you by reason of the exceeding grace of God in you.
units.rightText: while they themselves also, with supplication on your behalf, long after you by reason of the exceeding grace of God in you.

units.leftText: Now thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift!
units.rightText: Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift.

units.leftText: Now I Paul, myself, entreat you by the humility and gentleness of Christ, I who in your presence am lowly among you, but being absent am bold toward you.
units.rightText: Now I Paul myself entreat you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, I who in your presence am lowly among you, but being absent am of good courage toward you:

units.leftText: Yes, I beg you that I may not, when present, show courage with the confidence with which I intend to be bold against some, who consider us to be walking according to the flesh.
units.rightText: yea, I beseech you, that I may not when present show courage with the confidence wherewith I count to be bold against some, who count of us as if we walked according to the flesh.

units.leftText: For though we walk in the flesh, we don’t wage war according to the flesh;
units.rightText: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh

units.leftText: for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the throwing down of strongholds,
units.rightText: (for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the casting down of strongholds);

units.leftText: throwing down imaginations and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ,
units.rightText: casting down imaginations, and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God, and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ;

units.leftText: and being in readiness to avenge all disobedience when your obedience is made full.
units.rightText: and being in readiness to avenge all disobedience, when your obedience shall be made full.

units.leftText: Do you look at things only as they appear in front of your face? If anyone trusts in himself that he is Christ’s, let him consider this again with himself, that even as he is Christ’s, so we also are Christ’s.
units.rightText: Ye look at the things that are before your face. If any man trusteth in himself that he is Christ’s, let him consider this again with himself, that, even as he is Christ’s, so also are we.

units.leftText: For even if I boast somewhat abundantly concerning our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for casting you down, I will not be ashamed,
units.rightText: For though I should glory somewhat abundantly concerning our authority (which the Lord gave for building you up, and not for casting you down), I shall not be put to shame:

units.leftText: that I may not seem as if I desire to terrify you by my letters.
units.rightText: that I may not seem as if I would terrify you by my letters.

units.leftText: For, “His letters”, they say, “are weighty and strong, but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is despised.”
units.rightText: For, His letters, they say, are weighty and strong; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech of no account.

units.leftText: Let such a person consider this, that what we are in word by letters when we are absent, such are we also in deed when we are present.
units.rightText: Let such a one reckon this, that, what we are in word by letters when we are absent, such are we also in deed when we are present.

units.leftText: For we are not bold to number or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. But they themselves, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.
units.rightText: For we are not bold to number or compare ourselves with certain of them that commend themselves: but they themselves, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.

units.leftText: But we will not boast beyond proper limits, but within the boundaries with which God appointed to us, which reach even to you.
units.rightText: But we will not glory beyond our measure, but according to the measure of the province which God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even unto you.

units.leftText: For we don’t stretch ourselves too much, as though we didn’t reach to you. For we came even as far as to you with the Good News of Christ,
units.rightText: For we stretch not ourselves overmuch, as though we reached not unto you: for we came even as far as unto you in the gospel of Christ:

units.leftText: not boasting beyond proper limits in other men’s labors, but having hope that as your faith grows, we will be abundantly enlarged by you in our sphere of influence,
units.rightText: not glorying beyond our measure, that is, in other men’s labors; but having hope that, as your faith groweth, we shall be magnified in you according to our province unto further abundance,

units.leftText: so as to preach the Good News even to the parts beyond you, not to boast in what someone else has already done.
units.rightText: so as to preach the gospel even unto the parts beyond you, and not to glory in another’s province in regard of things ready to our hand.

units.leftText: But “he who boasts, let him boast in the Lord.”
units.rightText: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.

units.leftText: For it isn’t he who commends himself who is approved, but whom the Lord commends.
units.rightText: For not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.

units.leftText: I wish that you would bear with me in a little foolishness, but indeed you do bear with me.
units.rightText: Would that ye could bear with me in a little foolishness: but indeed ye do bear with me.

units.leftText: For I am jealous over you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you in marriage to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
units.rightText: For I am jealous over you with a godly jealousy: for I espoused you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.

units.leftText: But I am afraid that somehow, as the serpent deceived Eve in his craftiness, so your minds might be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.
units.rightText: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve in his craftiness, your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity and the purity that is toward Christ.

units.leftText: For if he who comes preaches another Jesus whom we didn’t preach, or if you receive a different spirit which you didn’t receive, or a different “good news” which you didn’t accept, you put up with that well enough.
units.rightText: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or if ye receive a different spirit, which ye did not receive, or a different gospel, which ye did not accept, ye do well to bear with him.

units.leftText: For I reckon that I am not at all behind the very best apostles.
units.rightText: For I reckon that I am not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.

units.leftText: But though I am unskilled in speech, yet I am not unskilled in knowledge. No, in every way we have been revealed to you in all things.
units.rightText: But though I be rude in speech, yet am I not in knowledge; nay, in every way have we made this manifest unto you in all things.

units.leftText: Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God’s Good News free of charge?
units.rightText: Or did I commit a sin in abasing myself that ye might be exalted, because I preached to you the gospel of God for nought?

units.leftText: I robbed other assemblies, taking wages from them that I might serve you.
units.rightText: I robbed other churches, taking wages of them that I might minister unto you;

units.leftText: When I was present with you and was in need, I wasn’t a burden on anyone, for the brothers, when they came from Macedonia, supplied the measure of my need. In everything I kept myself from being burdensome to you, and I will continue to do so.
units.rightText: and when I was present with you and was in want, I was not a burden on any man; for the brethren, when they came from Macedonia, supplied the measure of my want; and in everything I kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and so will I keep myself.

units.leftText: As the truth of Christ is in me, no one will stop me from this boasting in the regions of Achaia.
units.rightText: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this glorying in the regions of Achaia.

units.leftText: Why? Because I don’t love you? God knows.
units.rightText: Wherefore? because I love you not? God knoweth.

units.leftText: But what I do, that I will continue to do, that I may cut off opportunity from those who desire an opportunity, that in which they boast, they may be recognized just like us.
units.rightText: But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them that desire an occasion; that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we.

units.leftText: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as Christ’s apostles.
units.rightText: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, fashioning themselves into apostles of Christ.

units.leftText: And no wonder, for even Satan masquerades as an angel of light.
units.rightText: And no marvel; for even Satan fashioneth himself into an angel of light.

units.leftText: It is no great thing therefore if his servants also masquerade as servants of righteousness, whose end will be according to their works.
units.rightText: It is no great thing therefore if his ministers also fashion themselves as ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.

units.leftText: I say again, let no one think me foolish. But if so, yet receive me as foolish, that I also may boast a little.
units.rightText: I say again, Let no man think me foolish; but if ye do, yet as foolish receive me, that I also may glory a little.

units.leftText: That which I speak, I don’t speak according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of boasting.
units.rightText: That which I speak, I speak not after the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of glorying.

units.leftText: Seeing that many boast after the flesh, I will also boast.
units.rightText: Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.

units.leftText: For you bear with the foolish gladly, being wise.
units.rightText: For ye bear with the foolish gladly, being wise yourselves.

units.leftText: For you bear with a man if he brings you into bondage, if he devours you, if he takes you captive, if he exalts himself, or if he strikes you on the face.
units.rightText: For ye bear with a man, if he bringeth you into bondage, if he devoureth you, if he taketh you captive, if he exalteth himself, if he smiteth you on the face.

units.leftText: To my shame, I speak as though we had been weak. Yet in whatever way anyone is bold (I speak in foolishness), I am bold also.
units.rightText: I speak by way of disparagement, as though we had been weak. Yet whereinsoever any is bold (I speak in foolishness), I am bold also.

units.leftText: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the offspring of Abraham? So am I.
units.rightText: Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.

units.leftText: Are they servants of Christ? (I speak as one beside himself.) I am more so: in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, and in deaths often.
units.rightText: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as one beside himself) I more; in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, in deaths oft.

units.leftText: Five times I received forty stripes minus one from the Jews.
units.rightText: Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.

units.leftText: Three times I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Three times I suffered shipwreck. I have been a night and a day in the deep.
units.rightText: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day have I been in the deep;

units.leftText: I have been in travels often, perils of rivers, perils of robbers, perils from my countrymen, perils from the Gentiles, perils in the city, perils in the wilderness, perils in the sea, perils among false brothers;
units.rightText: in journeyings often, in perils of rivers, in perils of robbers, in perils from my countrymen, in perils from the Gentiles, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;

units.leftText: in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, and in cold and nakedness.
units.rightText: in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.

units.leftText: Besides those things that are outside, there is that which presses on me daily: anxiety for all the assemblies.
units.rightText: Besides those things that are without, there is that which presseth upon me daily, anxiety for all the churches.

units.leftText: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is caused to stumble, and I don’t burn with indignation?
units.rightText: Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is caused to stumble, and I burn not?

units.leftText: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that concern my weakness.
units.rightText: If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things that concern my weakness.

units.leftText: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus Christ, he who is blessed forever more, knows that I don’t lie.
units.rightText: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, he who is blessed for evermore knoweth that I lie not.

units.leftText: In Damascus the governor under King Aretas guarded the Damascenes’ city, desiring to arrest me.
units.rightText: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king guarded the city of the Damascenes in order to take me:

units.leftText: I was let down in a basket through a window by the wall, and escaped his hands.
units.rightText: and through a window was I let down in a basket by the wall, and escaped his hands.

units.leftText: It is doubtless not profitable for me to boast, but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
units.rightText: I must needs glory, though it is not expedient; but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.

units.leftText: I know a man in Christ who was caught up into the third heaven fourteen years ago—whether in the body, I don’t know, or whether out of the body, I don’t know; God knows.
units.rightText: I know a man in Christ, fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I know not; or whether out of the body, I know not; God knoweth), such a one caught up even to the third heaven.

units.leftText: I know such a man (whether in the body, or outside of the body, I don’t know; God knows),
units.rightText: And I know such a man (whether in the body, or apart from the body, I know not; God knoweth),

units.leftText: how he was caught up into Paradise and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
units.rightText: how that he was caught up into Paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.

units.leftText: On behalf of such a one I will boast, but on my own behalf I will not boast, except in my weaknesses.
units.rightText: On behalf of such a one will I glory: but on mine own behalf I will not glory, save in my weaknesses.

units.leftText: For if I would desire to boast, I will not be foolish; for I will speak the truth. But I refrain, so that no man may think more of me than that which he sees in me or hears from me.
units.rightText: For if I should desire to glory, I shall not be foolish; for I shall speak the truth: but I forbear, lest any man should account of me above that which he seeth me to be, or heareth from me.

units.leftText: By reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted excessively, a thorn in the flesh was given to me: a messenger of Satan to torment me, that I should not be exalted excessively.
units.rightText: And by reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted overmuch, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to buffet me, that I should not be exalted overmuch.

units.leftText: Concerning this thing, I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.
units.rightText: Concerning this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.

units.leftText: He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
units.rightText: And he hath said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my power is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

units.leftText: Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, and in distresses, for Christ’s sake. For when I am weak, then am I strong.
units.rightText: Wherefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

units.leftText: I have become foolish in boasting. You compelled me, for I ought to have been commended by you, for I am in no way inferior to the very best apostles, though I am nothing.
units.rightText: I am become foolish: ye compelled me; for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing was I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I am nothing.

units.leftText: Truly the signs of an apostle were worked among you in all perseverance, in signs and wonders and mighty works.
units.rightText: Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, by signs and wonders and mighty works.

units.leftText: For what is there in which you were made inferior to the rest of the assemblies, unless it is that I myself was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
units.rightText: For what is there wherein ye were made inferior to the rest of the churches, except it be that I myself was not a burden to you? forgive me this wrong.

units.leftText: Behold, this is the third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden to you; for I seek not your possessions, but you. For the children ought not to save up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
units.rightText: Behold, this is the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be a burden to you: for I seek not yours, but you: for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

units.leftText: I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I loved the less?
units.rightText: And I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I loved the less?

units.leftText: Even so, I myself didn’t burden you. But you might say that being crafty, I caught you with deception.
units.rightText: But be it so, I did not myself burden you; but, being crafty, I caught you with guile.

units.leftText: Did I take advantage of you by anyone of those whom I have sent to you?
units.rightText: Did I take advantage of you by any one of them whom I have sent unto you?

units.leftText: I exhorted Titus, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take any advantage of you? Didn’t we walk in the same spirit? Didn’t we walk in the same steps?
units.rightText: I exhorted Titus, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take any advantage of you? walked we not in the same spirit? walked we not in the same steps?

units.leftText: Again, do you think that we are excusing ourselves to you? In the sight of God we speak in Christ. But all things, beloved, are for your edifying.
units.rightText: Ye think all this time that we are excusing ourselves unto you. In the sight of God speak we in Christ. But all things, beloved, are for your edifying.

units.leftText: For I am afraid that perhaps when I come, I might find you not the way I want to, and that I might be found by you as you don’t desire, that perhaps there would be strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, factions, slander, whisperings, proud thoughts, or riots,
units.rightText: For I fear, lest by any means, when I come, I should find you not such as I would, and should myself be found of you such as ye would not; lest by any means there should be strife, jealousy, wraths, factions, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults;

units.leftText: that again when I come my God would humble me before you, and I would mourn for many of those who have sinned before now, and not repented of the uncleanness, sexual immorality, and lustfulness which they committed.
units.rightText: lest again when I come my God should humble me before you, and I should mourn for many of them that have sinned heretofore, and repented not of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they committed.

units.leftText: This is the third time I am coming to you. “At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.”
units.rightText: This is the third time I am coming to you. At the mouth of two witnesses or three shall every word be established.

units.leftText: I have warned previously, and I warn again, as when I was present the second time, so now, being absent, I write to those who have sinned before now and to all the rest that if I come again, I will not spare,
units.rightText: I have said beforehand, and I do say beforehand, as when I was present the second time, so now, being absent, to them that have sinned heretofore, and to all the rest, that, if I come again, I will not spare;

units.leftText: seeing that you seek a proof of Christ who speaks in me who is not weak, but is powerful in you.
units.rightText: seeing that ye seek a proof of Christ that speaketh in me; who to you-ward is not weak, but is powerful in you:

units.leftText: For he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives through the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we will live with him through the power of God toward you.
units.rightText: for he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth through the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him through the power of God toward you.

units.leftText: Examine your own selves, whether you are in the faith. Test your own selves. Or don’t you know about your own selves, that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless indeed you are disqualified.
units.rightText: Try your own selves, whether ye are in the faith; prove your own selves. Or know ye not as to your own selves, that Jesus Christ is in you? unless indeed ye be reprobate.

units.leftText: But I hope that you will know that we aren’t disqualified.
units.rightText: But I hope that ye shall know that we are not reprobate.

units.leftText: Now I pray to God that you do no evil; not that we may appear approved, but that you may do that which is honorable, though we may seem to have failed.
units.rightText: Now we pray to God that ye do no evil; not that we may appear approved, but that ye may do that which is honorable, though we be as reprobate.

units.leftText: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
units.rightText: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.

units.leftText: For we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong. We also pray for this: your becoming perfect.
units.rightText: For we rejoice, when we are weak, and ye are strong: this we also pray for, even your perfecting.

units.leftText: For this cause I write these things while absent, that I may not deal sharply when present, according to the authority which the Lord gave me for building up and not for tearing down.
units.rightText: For this cause I write these things while absent, that I may not when present deal sharply, according to the authority which the Lord gave me for building up, and not for casting down.

units.leftText: Finally, brothers, rejoice! Be perfected. Be comforted. Be of the same mind. Live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
units.rightText: Finally, brethren, farewell. Be perfected; be comforted; be of the same mind; live in peace: and the God of love and peace shall be with you.

units.leftText: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
units.rightText: Salute one another with a holy kiss.

units.leftText: All the saints greet you.
units.rightText: All the saints salute you.

units.leftText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, God’s love, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.
units.rightText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit, be with you all.
